creator: Anonymous
model: Circular fluid-driven frictional rupture of Sáez, Lecampion, Bhattacharya and Viesca (2022): planar homogeneous permeable fault layer with linear pressure diffusion (diffusivity alpha) from a point source or a fixed Gaussian source of width parameter epsilon; zero Poisson ratio; uniform constant friction f; zero fracture energy; uniform positive strength excess tau_d = f sigma'_0 - tau_0; one-way coupling from pressure to slip; crack radius R(t) from the zero-stress-intensity condition f A p(R,t) = tau_d; injection rate q(t) >= 0.

definitions.fullSliding: the trial (circular) slip rate is nonnegative at every point of the disk
definitions.centreMargin: C(t): the centre slip rate of the trial branch divided by the positive factor 4 f c_p/(pi mu), equation (13)
definitions.lossOfFullSliding: the first negative crossing of the centre margin (or, for a point source, a downward rate jump); a zero alone is threshold contact

claims.statement: For a point source, a Gaussian source or any positive mixture of Gaussian widths and a single-peaked (rise-then-fall) injection rate, at any time with a positive crack radius, the slip rate is nonnegative throughout the disk if and only if the centre margin is nonnegative; strictly so off the centre under a measure condition. The trajectory form requires the centre test at every time from the start of slip.
claims.evidence: written proof (Lemma 2, Appendix A); verify_kernel_order.py, verify_fault_criterion.py

claims.location: Theorems A and B, Proposition 4.1, Appendix B
claims.statement: Point source, piecewise-C^1 rate with positive initial rate or a nondecreasing start: full sliding holds throughout (0,T] (away from jump times) if and only if the centre margin has stayed nonnegative there; the crack radius then exists and strictly increases; any downward jump before T ends full sliding at once; within these startup classes and with no downward jump before the contact, full sliding is first lost at the centre.

Gaussian source, piecewise-C^1 rate with jumps of either sign, nonnegative latent forcing before slip starts and transverse nucleation: the same equivalence and centre-first conclusion as C2 from nucleation onward.

After a constant-rate stage of duration T with a Gaussian source, an abrupt relative drop j/q0 ends full sliding exactly when it exceeds the kernel ratio K_R(0,T+eps)/K_R(0,eps), bounded above by sqrt(eps/(T+eps)); about 1e-3 at wellbore scale for illustrative parameters.

The constructed trial branch satisfies the friction inequality outside the disk; in a stated variational forward-slip class it is unique up to first failure for the Gaussian source (admissibility but not uniqueness claimed for the point source).

Inner (critically stressed, Theta -> 0) limit, point source, bounded-variation history: the slip rate at radius r is the centre slip rate delayed by a random diffusive first-passage time (probability measure Lambda_r), so a nonnegative centre history is necessary and sufficient for full sliding.

Uniform finite-radius error bound with constant 4 alpha s*/R and a two-term centre margin A_* Hq(t) - (2 alpha/R) q(t-) with rigorous remainder (16 c_D alpha^2/(3R^3)) int (t-s)|dq|, using numerically verified bounds s* <= 0.6424 and c_D <= 0.4115.
claims.evidence: written proof with numerically verified constants; constants_and_two_term.py

claims.statement: After shut-in at t_s with injected volume V (either source, startup as Theorem A or G), no crack exists after t_s + f c_p V/tau_d - eps, and full sliding is lost before then; after a constant-rate stage of duration T this is T(1 + 1/Theta) - eps.

Point source, constant first stage followed by a linear taper: in the inner limit the admissible taper depth is at most (1/2) sqrt(L/(T+L)) < 1/2, and strictly smaller at every finite radius; hence no linear taper can halve the rate without loss of full sliding. The arcsine continuation is the slowest admissible continuation in the inner limit.

numericalOnly: Finite-radius taper thresholds d_max(Theta) and taper roots (finite-window estimates, Tables 2-3)
Leading-order taper formula (54) (approximation, error below 0.033 Theta for Theta <= 0.1 on the computed grid)
Two-dip, stepped Gaussian, upward-jump and multi-peak examples (Section 9.3)
Annular-source time history (numerical evidence of off-centre reversal)
counterexamples: The pairwise radial order (total positivity in (r,u)) is false (Section 9.4)
An instantaneous centre test is not sufficient for general histories (Section 9.4)
An annular source violates the age order and the centre-first property (Section 9.4)
scopeLimits: Zero Poisson ratio, constant friction, zero fracture energy, homogeneous layer, one-way coupling
First loss of full sliding only; no claim about the later slip pulse or seismic hazard
Gaussian histories with decreasing centre pressure before nucleation are open
Point-source results are elastic statements on r > 0
